indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so the jumbled letters wrap round the bill
something that has suffered has been knocked about, so the letters of heather are jumbled

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone named Heather went through grief while protecting a bird's beak, or perhaps an unpaid invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name, but 'suffered' marks it as anagram fodder, and 'sheltering' makes its rearrangement wrap round the account abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is deep sorrow or anguish, the same feeling as grief.

clue.text: It was hell before public transport

parts.note: ere is an old poetic word for before
a bus is a vehicle of public transport

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that travelling before buses existed was a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of the underworld that the dead pass through, so 'hell' is fair, with 'was' fitting the ancient myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erebus is the place of darkness in Greek mythology, a region of the underworld akin to Hades.

clue.text: Again make an impression in the pool

definitions.text: Again make an impression in the pool

parts.words: Again make an impression in the pool
parts.note: the typing pool was the office room of typists; to strike the keys once more to print a page is to make an impression again

explanation.surface: Someone dives back into a swimming pool hoping to impress onlookers a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is not for swimming: it is the old office typing pool, and a key striking paper makes an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To key a document a second time on a typewriter is to print its letters again.

clue.text: Painter or professional performer for the most part

indicators.note: taking most of a word means dropping its last letter, here from the stage performer

parts.note: an artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a painter is really mostly just a show-off performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the final E from ARTISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist is anyone who paints pictures, among other creative crafts.

clue.text: How bowling side might be enjoying period of exciting activity

definitions.meaning: in cricket the side that bowls is out in the field, so a fielding team could be said to have a day in the field
a lively time of great fun or success, often at someone else's expense

explanation.surface: A cricket team that is fielding is said to be having a thoroughly exciting time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowling side is the fielding side, which the literal reading of the idiom fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a time of great enjoyment or unrestrained activity, while literally a fielding team spends its day on the pitch.

clue.text: Safe place railway worker found for member of volunteer force

parts.note: home is the safe base in many children's games, and a safe refuge generally
a guard is the railway employee in charge of a train

explanation.surface: A railway employee finds safety by joining a wartime band of volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer defence force in the Second World War, and one of its members was also called a home guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Britain's wartime local defence militia were known by the name of the force itself.

definitions.meaning: a character is an odd or colourful person
behaving in an unconventional or strange way

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person whose behaviour departs from what is usual.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconventional, odd person is called a character, and such behaviour is described as quirky or departing from the norm.

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the words that follow, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was pulled to safety out of a deep river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a drowning rescue; in fact 'from' signals that DEEP RIVER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reprieved is to be saved at the last moment from a threatened fate, a close synonym of rescued.

indicators.note: first tells us the short name goes in front of the revolutionary

parts.note: Lou is a short form of the name Louise
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary in crosswords

explanation.surface: A woman named Louise, once a revolutionary, turns into a menacing figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or shady, close in sense to sinister.

clue.text: Experimental shelter took in about four

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter

indicators.note: about means going round, so the eating word goes round the number

parts.note: to take in food is to eat it, so took in gives ate
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone trying out a new shelter crams about four people inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took in' reads as a containment signal but is the past tense of eating; it is 'about' that does the wrapping, round the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentative plan is provisional and done as a trial, which is what experimental means.

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word is heard rather than read, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: meatier means having more flesh

explanation.surface: Someone asks which celestial object is the more substantial and fleshy.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud in a British accent, MEATIER and METEOR are close; 'sounding' signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a heavenly body, a piece of space rock burning up in the sky.

definitions.meaning: used to put forward a suggestion, as in 'what if we went?'
assuming or imagining something without proof

explanation.definitionFit: It can open a suggestion like 'what if we tried this?', and it also means assuming or conjecturing.

clue.text: Reptile let loose after furrow was turned over

indicators.note: after puts the loosened word behind the furrow
turning over a word means reading it backwards, so the furrow is reversed

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow

indicators.note: let loose means the letters of let are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A reptile was released after a field furrow had been ploughed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was turned over' reverses the groove, and 'loose' scrambles the three-letter word, which 'after' places behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turtles are shelled reptiles living in water.

clue.text: Time of danger on loch — vigilance required

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the warning word sits on top of the loch

parts.note: an alert is a period of warning when danger threatens, as in an air-raid alert
Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A dangerous spell on a Scottish lake calls for watchfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is the Scottish lake famous for its monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Alertness is watchful readiness, the same as vigilance.

definitions.meaning: jokingly, in a meal's course, the soup being one of them

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in serious trouble, and literally something sitting in a bowl at the first course of a meal.

indicators.note: read as re-moving, the letters are moved again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone opens a game by taking away a cunning move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' looks like a deletion but is read as re-moving, rearranging the letters of START GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or ruse, so a trick.

clue.text: Penny took gold from Pyrenean tourist centre

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone named Penny carried off gold from a holiday town in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Pau is a town in south-west France, at the foot of the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pau is a French resort town popular with visitors for its views of the mountains.

indicators.note: inside puts the egg shape within the platinum symbol

parts.note: Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum
O, being egg-shaped, can stand for an egg

explanation.surface: An egg is discovered inside a container made of platinum.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a deep container used for cooking, a vessel.

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the word spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: U's, the plural of the letter U, are letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to do with some letters, perhaps writing them.
explanation.walkthrough: U's, as in more than one letter U, is pronounced like the verb USE.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a thing is to employ it or put it to work.

clue.text: One may be rewarded for an hour in church perhaps

definitions.text: One may be rewarded for an hour in church perhaps

parts.words: One may be rewarded for an hour in church perhaps
parts.note: a worship meeting might last an hour, and staff are often rewarded for long years of work for an employer

explanation.surface: A churchgoer hopes to earn some reward for sitting through an hour of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means time worked for an employer; read literally it is how long a church service lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the time worked for an employer, which can bring rewards, but literally the duration of a church service.

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word for layer

parts.note: a tier is a layer or level, as of a cake

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a layer that goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the final R from TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a game that ends level, a draw.

clue.text: You cannot do this if it has not been warm previously

definitions.text: You cannot do this if it has not been warm previously

parts.words: You cannot do this if it has not been warm previously
parts.note: warming food again only makes sense if it was hot before

explanation.surface: A cook points out something that is impossible unless the food was hot once already.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm leftovers again presupposes they were hot before.

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A clever circle of friends had a powerful drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Stingo is an old word for a strong beer or ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is a dialect word for a potent ale.

parts.note: interrupting a speaker with jeers stops them talking freely

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of censorship, blocking free expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests censorship; the answer is a barracker's interruptions that stop a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack a public speaker with jeers and interruptions prevents them speaking freely.

clue.text: Express grief when man shortly captures old bird

indicators.note: captures means the man holds the bird inside himself

parts.note: Ben is a short form of the man's name Benjamin
the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: Someone grieves when a man briefly catches an aged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' places the extinct New Zealand bird inside the abbreviated name; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan is to lament or complain about something, voicing sorrow.

clue.text: One who praises loudly the last one mentioned with hesitation

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction meaning loudly
the latter is the second or last of things just named
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone praises loudly whatever was mentioned last, while hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: F is short for forte, the musical marking for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatterer is a person who heaps excessive compliments on others.

indicators.note: round means the rearranged name goes around the a
travelled suggests the letters of Susan have moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Susan journeyed around a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelled' rearranges SUSAN and 'round' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas.

parts.note: a phrase admitting lack of knowledge, also exclaimed in astonishment, as in 'well, I never'

explanation.surface: Someone shows a lack of knowledge in an exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase confesses ignorance and is also exclaimed in amazement.

parts.note: a cup-bearer was a royal servant, but literally a small plate bears a cup

explanation.definitionFit: A small dish that holds a teacup underneath it bears the cup.

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of many bones are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists that not many bones were broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges MANY BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic denial, meaning not at all.
